text: Identify the adult worm and how it causes internal autoinfection:
options: Echinococcus granulosus - a ruptured hydatid cyst releases protoscolices that grow into adults
Diphyllobothrium latum - plerocercoids develop in the intestinal wall
Taenia saginata - reverse peristalsis carries gravid segments to the stomach
Hymenolepis nana - eggs hatch in the intestine and oncospheres develop into cysticercoids in the villi
Hymenolepis nana - it does not cause autoinfection; a flea or beetle intermediate host is obligatory
explanation:
Criteria of Identification: Hymenolepis nana (dwarf tapeworm) is the only human cestode capable of internal autoinfection: eggs released in the small intestine can hatch prematurely without exiting the body. The released hexacanth oncospheres penetrate the intestinal villi, develop into cysticercoids, and re-emerge into the lumen to mature into adult worms, perpetuating heavy worm burdens.

Option A is incorrect because hydatid cyst protoscolices develop into adults only in canine definitive hosts. Option C is incorrect because T. saginata does not cause human cysticercosis or autoinfection.
keyConcept: Hymenolepis nana: Only cestode with internal autoinfection (eggs hatch in lumen, cysticercoids in villi).

text: Structure 2 in this specimen is composed of:
options: Numerous follicular testes scattered in the body
explanation:
Criteria of Identification: The male Schistosoma mansoni possesses 6 to 9 testes arranged in a compact zigzag cluster situated dorsally near the anterior end behind the ventral sucker. In contrast, S. haematobium has 4 to 5 testes in a straight line.

Option A describes female flukes. Option C describes cestodes. Option E describes Fasciola (two deeply branched testes).
keyConcept: Male Schistosoma mansoni is characterized by 6–9 testes clustered behind the ventral sucker.

text: A carrier of an adult tapeworm developed cysticercosis through autoinfection. Which figure shows the gravid segment of his worm?
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Human cysticercosis occurs exclusively with Taenia solium (the pork tapeworm), never Taenia saginata. A patient harboring an adult T. solium can develop cysticercosis through external autoinfection (fecal-oral ingestion of gravid eggs) or internal autoinfection (reverse peristalsis carrying gravid segments into the stomach, where gastric acid digests the egg shell).
keyConcept: Taenia solium causes human cysticercosis via autoinfection; T. saginata does not.

text: Rectal prolapse is a complication of heavy infection with this worm. Interpret.
options: Chronic blood loss causes atrophy of the anal sphincter
Gravid females migrate out at night, causing straining during sleep
A bolus of entangled adult worms obstructs the rectum and pushes it outwards
Flask-shaped ulcers weaken the rectal wall
The worm is deeply embedded in the mucosa by its thin anterior part, causing loss of muscle tone in heavy infection
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Rectal prolapse is a hallmark complication of heavy Trichuris trichiura (whipworm) infection (Trichuris Dysentery Syndrome) in malnourished children. Thousands of adult worms embed their thread-like anterior ends into the cecal and rectal mucosa, causing intense inflammation, tenesmus, and chronic straining that precipitates rectal prolapse.
keyConcept: Heavy Trichuris trichiura (whipworm) infection causes rectal prolapse in children due to severe tenesmus.

text: Identify the station and its identifying criterion:
options: Entamoeba coli cyst - up to 8 nuclei with eccentric karyosomes
Entamoeba histolytica cyst - 1-4 nuclei with central karyosomes
Giardia lamblia cyst - 4 nuclei and axostyles
Entamoeba histolytica cyst - up to 8 nuclei with central karyosomes
explanation: Criteria of Identification: The mature cyst of Entamoeba histolytica measures 10–15 µm, contains 1 to 4 vesicular nuclei with fine, centrally placed karyosomes and evenly distributed peripheral chromatin, and often displays rod-shaped chromatoid bars with rounded ends. Entamoeba coli cysts contain up to 8 nuclei with eccentric karyosomes.
keyConcept: Entamoeba histolytica cyst: 1–4 nuclei, small central karyosome, rounded chromatoid bodies.

text: Identify the station and its relevance to man:
options: Cysticercus bovis - it causes human cysticercosis after eating the eggs
Hydatid cyst - man is an accidental intermediate host
Cysticercoid of H. nana - it develops in the human intestinal villi
Cysticercus cellulosae - it can develop in the human brain
Cysticercus bovis - man is infected by eating it in undercooked beef, but it does not develop in man
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Hydatid disease (cystic echinococcosis) is caused by the larval stage of Echinococcus granulosus. Dogs and canids are the definitive hosts harboring adult worms; sheep and herbivores are natural intermediate hosts. Humans become accidental intermediate hosts by ingesting eggs passed in dog feces.
keyConcept: Echinococcus granulosus: Humans are accidental dead-end intermediate hosts harboring hydatid cysts.

text: This parasite may cause megaloblastic anemia. Interpret.
options: The adult worm sucks blood from the intestinal mucosa
The adult worm in the small intestine takes up large amounts of dietary vitamin B12
The eggs embolize to the bone marrow
Larvae invade the stomach and destroy the parietal cells
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Diphyllobothrium latum (the broad fish tapeworm) resides in the ileum and actively absorbs massive quantities of host dietary vitamin B12 (up to 80–100%), depriving the human host and producing megaloblastic / pernicious-like anemia with subacute combined degeneration of the spinal cord.
keyConcept: Diphyllobothrium latum causes megaloblastic anemia by competing for dietary vitamin B12 in the ileum.

text: All of the following eggs are mature EXCEPT:
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Fasciola and Ascaris eggs are passed unembryonated (immature) in fresh stool, requiring external development in water or moist soil before becoming infective. In contrast, Enterobius and Heterophyes eggs are passed fully embryonated (mature).
keyConcept: Fasciola, Ascaris, and Hookworm eggs are passed immature (unsegmented) in stool.

text: Food handlers are a serious source of this infection. Yes or No? Justify.
options: No - the infection is transmitted only through water
No - the cyst must mature in soil before it becomes infective
Yes - asymptomatic carriers pass mature quadrinucleate cysts that are infective on passage and contaminate food
Yes - trophozoites survive on food and invade the colon
No - only trophozoites are passed, and they die quickly outside the body
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Cysts of Entamoeba histolytica and Giardia lamblia are immediately infective upon excretion and are resistant to environmental chlorination. Chronic carriers working as food handlers readily transmit cysts to food or beverages via contaminated, unwashed hands.
keyConcept: Entamoeba and Giardia cysts are directly infective upon passage, making food handlers key vectors.

text: Structure 3 in this specimen is the:
explanation: Criteria of Identification: The gynecophoric canal is the deep longitudinal ventral groove formed by the folded lateral margins of the male Schistosoma worm, in which the slender female fluke is embraced during copulation and egg laying.
keyConcept: Schistosoma male: Gynecophoric canal embraces the slender female during copulation.

text: This patient was admitted with diarrhea and abdominal pain. His skin had a diffuse, rapidly moving, erythematous reticular rash from the anal margin to the upper legs. Which figure represents the stage found on stool examination?
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Trophozoites of Giardia lamblia colonize the duodenal and jejunal brush border, causing malabsorption, foul-smelling steatorrhea, and epigastric cramping without mucosal ulceration or blood.
keyConcept: Giardia lamblia: Duodenal colonization causes watery/fatty non-bloody diarrhea and malabsorption.

text: Identify the station and the main reservoir of infection:
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Balantidium coli is the largest protozoan and the only pathogenic ciliate infecting humans. Domestic pigs serve as the primary animal reservoir. Human infection occurs via ingestion of large cysts contaminating water or vegetables in pig-farming areas.
keyConcept: Balantidium coli: Giant ciliated protozoan; pigs are the main natural reservoir host.

text: A 31-year-old HIV-infected woman presents with severe watery diarrhea and dizziness. Which figure represents the stage found on stool examination?
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Cryptosporidium parvum is an opportunistic apicomplexan protozoan causing chronic, life-threatening, cholera-like watery diarrhea and severe dehydration in immunocompromised patients (especially HIV with CD4 < 100/µL). Diagnosis is made by identifying 4–5 µm acid-fast spherical oocysts.
keyConcept: Cryptosporidium parvum causes chronic intractable watery diarrhea in immunocompromised / HIV patients.

text: Identify this egg:
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Enterobius vermicularis (pinworm) eggs are characteristically planoconvex (flattened on one side and convex on the other, 'D-shaped'), measuring 50–60 × 20–30 µm, possessing a smooth double-contoured translucent shell containing a fully formed tadpole-like coiled larva.
keyConcept: Enterobius vermicularis egg: D-shaped (planoconvex), colorless translucent shell with coiled larva.

text: Identify the station and the arrowed structure:
options: Taenia spp. mature segment - bilobed ovary
Taenia saginata gravid segment - central uterine stem
Taenia solium gravid segment - lateral uterine branches
Diphyllobothrium latum mature segment - rosette-shaped uterus
Diphyllobothrium latum mature segment - bilobed ovary
explanation: Criteria of Identification: In mature proglottids of Taenia, the female reproductive organs are dominated by a prominent bilobed ovary situated in the posterior third of the segment, along with numerous follicular testes scattered throughout and a lateral genital pore.
keyConcept: Taenia mature segment: Bilobed ovary, median tubular uterus, and scattered follicular testes.

text: Identify the station:
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Gravid proglottids of Taenia saginata are distinguished from Taenia solium by counting the primary lateral uterine branches on each side of the central stem: T. saginata has 15 to 30 branches (dichotomous branching), whereas T. solium has only 7 to 12 branches (dendritic branching).
keyConcept: Taenia saginata gravid segment: 15–30 main lateral uterine branches on each side.

text: A child presents with appendicitis. Which of the following parasites can cause it?
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Adult Enterobius vermicularis pinworms frequently inhabit the cecum and vermiform appendix. In children presenting with symptoms of acute or subacute appendicitis, pinworms in the appendiceal lumen can cause mechanical obstruction or mucosal pin-prick lesions mimicking appendicitis.
keyConcept: Enterobius vermicularis is the most common helminth discovered inside surgical appendectomy specimens.

text: An Egyptian farmer presented with hematemesis, hepatosplenomegaly and ascites. Sonography showed severe periportal fibrosis. Which figure represents the stage found on stool examination during the acute stage?
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Schistosoma mansoni adult worms reside in the inferior mesenteric veins. Embolized eggs lodge in the periportal hepatic venules, triggering granulomatous inflammation, Symmers' clay-pipe-stem fibrosis, non-cirrhotic presinusoidal portal hypertension, splenomegaly, and bleeding esophageal varices (hematemesis).
keyConcept: Schistosoma mansoni causes Symmers' clay-pipe-stem portal fibrosis, splenomegaly, and esophageal varices.

text: Identify the station:
options: Balantidium coli cyst invading the mucosa
Cryptosporidium parvum stages on the brush border
Balantidium coli trophozoite at the brush border
Balantidium coli cyst at the brush border
Balantidium coli trophozoites invading the mucosa
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Cryptosporidium parvum occupies an intracellular but extracytoplasmic position directly within the brush border of intestinal epithelial enterocytes, enclosed in a host-derived parasitophorous vacuole that blunts microvilli and impairs absorption.
keyConcept: Cryptosporidium parvum lives intracellularly but extracytoplasmically on the enterocyte brush border.

text: The structure indicated by the upper arrow is the:
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Ancylostoma duodenale possesses a large chitinous buccal capsule equipped on its ventral margin with two pairs of curved pointed teeth, used to lacerate mucosal villi and ingest blood from the small intestinal mucosa.
keyConcept: Ancylostoma duodenale buccal capsule contains two pairs of sharp ventral teeth.

text: This parasitic stage emerges from:
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Furcocercous (forked-tail) cercariae of Schistosoma mansoni emerge directly from the freshwater snail Biomphalaria alexandrina (discoidal flat snail) and actively penetrate human intact skin in canal water.
keyConcept: Schistosoma mansoni forked-tail cercariae emerge from the intermediate snail Biomphalaria alexandrina.

text: Which of the following eggs is passed mature?
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Enterobius vermicularis and Heterophyes heterophyes eggs are passed fully mature (containing a fully developed larva or miracidium) and are immediately infective.
keyConcept: Enterobius and Heterophyes eggs are passed mature (containing fully developed embryos).

text: Chronic blood loss in this infection is multifactorial. Interpret.
options: The worm competes with the host for vitamin B12 and folate in the jejunum
The worm sucks blood, and leaving bleeding points
Larvae damage the lung capillaries, causing repeated hemoptysis
Larvae migrate through the liver, causing bleeding esophageal varices
The worm secretes a hemolysin that lyses red cells inside the portal vessels
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Hookworms cause microcytic hypochromic iron-deficiency anemia through two synergistic mechanisms: direct ingestion of blood by the worm (0.15–0.2 mL/day per worm) and persistent capillary oozing from mucosal bite sites due to secreted anticoagulant (acetylcholinesterase and calreticulin).
keyConcept: Hookworm anemia: Mechanical villous laceration, active blood ingestion, and anticoagulant-mediated oozing.

text: Identify the station and the feature that identifies it:
options: Trichocephalus trichiurus in the appendix - bacillary band
Enterobius vermicularis in the appendix - double-bulbed esophagus seen in section
Enterobius vermicularis in the appendix - lateral cuticular alae
Ascaris lumbricoides in the appendix - thick cuticle
Strongyloides stercoralis in the mucosa - eggs in the uterus
explanation: Criteria of Identification: On histological transverse sections of the appendix, Enterobius vermicularis is definitively identified by two diagnostic lateral cuticular alae (cristae) extending along the body and a muscular double-bulbed esophagus (corpus, isthmus, and spherical posterior bulb).
keyConcept: Enterobius vermicularis in appendix section: Bilateral pointed cuticular alae and double-bulbed esophagus.

text: Perianal swabbing is the method of choice for diagnosing infection with this egg. Interpret.
options: The eggs are very light and are lost from the surface of the stool sample
The gravid female migrates out of the anus at night and lays her eggs on the perianal skin,
Larvae from these eggs penetrate the perianal skin and stay there
The eggs hatch inside the colon, so only larvae reach the stool
The eggs are digested by colonic bacteria before they are passed
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Gravid female Enterobius vermicularis worms migrate out through the anal sphincter at night (when body temperature drops and the host rests) to deposit up to 15,000 sticky eggs on the perianal and perineal skin folds. Because eggs are laid outside the rectum, routine fecal examination is negative in 95% of cases.
keyConcept: Scotch tape test is diagnostic for Enterobius because gravid females oviposit on perianal skin at night.

text: Identify the arrowed stage. Why is it infective as soon as it is passed?
options: Giardia lamblia cyst - it already has 4 nuclei
Entamoeba histolytica cyst - it is mature with 4 nuclei
Cryptosporidium parvum oocyst - it sporulates in the colon after 24 hours
Cryptosporidium parvum oocyst - it is passed already sporulated, containing 4 sporozoites
Cryptosporidium parvum oocyst - it contains 8 merozoites
explanation: Criteria of Identification: The mature infective cyst of Giardia lamblia is oval, measures 8–12 µm, possesses a distinct smooth cyst wall separated from the cytoplasm by a clear space, and contains 4 spherical nuclei along with longitudinal curved axostyles and claw-shaped median bodies.
keyConcept: Giardia lamblia mature cyst: Oval shape, distinct cyst wall, 4 nuclei, and curved central axostyles.

text: The stage found inside this egg is:
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Inside the thick, radially striated, brown embryophore of a Taenia egg lies a spherical hexacanth embryo (oncosphere) bearing 6 chitinous hooklets (3 pairs).
keyConcept: Taenia egg contains a hexacanth embryo (oncosphere) equipped with 6 hooklets.

text: Identify the station and what this stage does after leaving the snail:
options: Leptocercus cercaria of Heterophyes - encysts in fish muscle
Leptocercus cercaria of Fasciola - penetrates human skin
Furcocercus cercaria of Schistosoma - encysts on aquatic plants
Furcocercus cercaria of Schistosoma - penetrates human skin
Leptocercus cercaria of Fasciola - encysts on aquatic plants as a metacercaria
explanation: Criteria of Identification: The lophocercous (pleurocercous) cercaria of Heterophyes heterophyes possesses a dorsal natatory fin-fold. After emerging from Pirenella conica snails, it penetrates and encysts as an infective metacercaria in the flesh of brackish-water fish (Bouri / mullet and Bolti / tilapia).
keyConcept: Heterophyes heterophyes cercaria encysts as infective metacercariae in freshwater/brackish fish.

text: A patient has fever, tenesmus and dysentery. Sigmoidoscopy shows ulcers with a narrow opening, raised edge and wide base. Which figure represents the stage found in the ulcer biopsy?
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Acute amoebic dysentery presents with bloody-mucoid stool, lower abdominal cramping, and tenesmus without high toxic fever, demonstrating flask-shaped mucosal ulcers on sigmoidoscopy.
keyConcept: Amoebic dysentery: Stool with blood and mucus, flask-shaped ulcers, trophozoites with ingested RBCs.

text: Growth retardation may be a manifestation of this parasitic infection. Interpret.
options: A bolus of adult worms causes intestinal obstruction
The adult worm absorbs most of the dietary vitamin B12
Autoinfective larvae destroy the intestinal villi
Egg granulomas cause periportal hepatic fibrosis
explanation: Criteria of Identification: In children, heavy Ascaris lumbricoides worm loads contribute to protein-energy malnutrition, vitamin A deficiency, and stunting due to mechanical competition for ingested nutrients and antiprotease enzyme secretion.
keyConcept: Heavy Ascaris burden leads to growth stunting and malnutrition in infected children.

text: Autoinfection is a recognized means of transmission of this parasite. Yes or No? Justify.
options: No - the egg must pass through a snail intermediate host
No - the egg must embryonate in moist soil for 2-3 weeks before it is infective
Yes - the larva inside the egg becomes infective within about 6 hours on the perianal skin, and scratching carries eggs to the mouth
Yes - rhabditiform larvae become filariform larvae inside the intestine
Yes - the egg hatches in the colon and the larva penetrates the colonic wall
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Enterobius vermicularis undergoes external autoinfection (hand-to-mouth via pruritus ani fingernail scratching) because eggs embryonate and become infective within 4–6 hours of oviposition on the warm perianal skin.
keyConcept: Enterobius vermicularis: Rapid perianal embryonation (4–6 hrs) drives hand-to-mouth autoinfection.

text: Identify the station and the arrowed structure:
options: Anterior end of Enterobius - cephalic ala
explanation: Criteria of Identification: The scolex of Diphyllobothrium latum is elongated and almond-shaped, lacking cup-like suckers and rostellum, characterized instead by two deep longitudinal suction grooves called bothria (one dorsal, one ventral).
keyConcept: Diphyllobothrium latum scolex: Almond-shaped with two longitudinal sucking grooves (bothria).

text: This parasite causes flask-shaped intestinal ulcers and extra-intestinal manifestations. Interpret.
options: Trophozoites lyse the mucosa with proteolytic enzymes, spread laterally in the submucosa, and reach the liver through the portal vein
Eggs lodge in the bowel wall and cause granulomas that ulcerate
Adult worms embed their anterior ends deep in the mucosa
Trophozoites burrow with their cilia and invade the lymphatics
Cysts excyst in the submucosa and grow into large colonies
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Entamoeba histolytica trophozoites adhere to colonic mucin via Gal/GalNAc lectin, secrete pore-forming amoebapore and cysteine proteases (histolysin) to lyse epithelial cells, and expand laterally in the loose submucosa, generating classic flask-shaped ulcers.
keyConcept: Entamoeba histolytica produces flask-shaped colonic ulcers via cysteine proteases and amoebapore.

text: The middle arrow points to a structure that distinguishes this fluke from Metagonimus yokogawai. It is the:
explanation: Criteria of Identification: The egg of Hymenolepis nana is round to oval, measures 45–50 µm, has two membranes (thin outer shell and thick inner embryophore), and is definitively identified by 4 to 8 hair-like polar filaments originating from mammillated polar thickenings and spreading into the space between membranes.
keyConcept: Hymenolepis nana egg: Hexacanth embryo with 4–8 wavy polar filaments emerging from polar knobs.

text: The stage found inside this egg is:
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Pirenella conica is a small, elongated, turreted conical brackish-water snail inhabiting Northern Egyptian lakes (Manzala, Burullus, Edku) that acts as the essential first intermediate host of Heterophyes heterophyes.
keyConcept: Pirenella conica is the first intermediate snail host of Heterophyes heterophyes in Egyptian lakes.

text: Identify the station:
options: Female of Strongyloides stercoralis with eggs in uterus
Female of Enterobius vermicularis with eggs in uterus
explanation: Criteria of Identification: The scolex of Hymenolepis nana is tiny (0.3 mm), subglobular, featuring 4 cup-like suckers and a single prominent retractable rostellum armed with a single circle of 20 to 30 tuning-fork hooklets.
keyConcept: Hymenolepis nana scolex: 4 spherical suckers and a retractable rostellum with 20–30 hooklets.

text: Structure 1 in this segment is the:
explanation: Criteria of Identification: The posterior end of the male Ancylostoma duodenale expands into an umbrella-shaped membranous copulatory bursa supported by fleshy rays (1 dorsal, 2 lateral lobes) and two long, slender spicules used during mating.
keyConcept: Male hookworm is identified by its posterior umbrella-shaped copulatory bursa supported by rays.

text: The stage found inside this egg is:
options: Immature ovum surrounded by yolk cells
explanation: Criteria of Identification: The egg of Trichuris trichiura is brown, barrel-shaped (lemon-shaped), measures 50 × 22 µm, possesses a thick smooth triple-layered shell, and is characterized by a prominent transparent mucoid plug at each pole.
keyConcept: Trichuris trichiura egg: Barrel-shaped, brown, with clear bipolar mucoid plugs.

text: An abdominal CT of a shepherd with right upper abdominal pain and no fever shows multiple cystic lesions of different sizes in both liver lobes. Which figure represents the stage found when the cyst fluid is examined?
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Typical fertilized Ascaris lumbricoides eggs are oval, measure 60–75 × 40–50 µm, enclosed by a thick transparent shell surrounded by a characteristic coarse, golden-brown, bile-stained mamillated albuminous outer coat.
keyConcept: Ascaris lumbricoides fertilized egg: Golden-brown, bile-stained, with a coarse mamillated coat.

text: All of the following parasites can cause appendicitis EXCEPT:
explanation: Criteria of Identification: The scolex of Taenia saginata (beef tapeworm) is quadrate (1.5–2 mm), equipped with 4 prominent hemispherical suckers, but is completely UNARMED (lacks both a rostellum and hooklets), distinguishing it from T. solium.
keyConcept: Taenia saginata scolex: 4 suckers, unarmed (no rostellum, no hooks).

text: Identify the station and the arrowed structure:
options: Entamoeba histolytica cyst - nucleus with central karyosome
Entamoeba histolytica trophozoite - nucleus with central karyosome
Entamoeba coli trophozoite - nucleus with eccentric karyosome
Entamoeba coli trophozoite - nucleus with central karyosome
explanation: Criteria of Identification: The egg of Schistosoma mansoni is large (115–175 × 45–70 µm), non-operculated, golden-yellow, and features a prominent, sharp, backward-pointing LATERAL spine near the posterior pole, containing a fully formed miracidium.
keyConcept: Schistosoma mansoni egg: Large, oval, golden-yellow, with a sharp prominent LATERAL spine.

text: A patient has hepatomegaly and jaundice. Three months ago he had fever, right upper quadrant pain and eosinophilia after eating green salads. Which figure represents the stage found on stool examination?
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Fasciola gigantica is a giant liver fluke measuring 25–75 × 12 mm, characterized by an elongated lanceolate leaf-like body, a small cephalic cone with indistinct shoulders, and extensively branched intestinal caeca and testes.
keyConcept: Fasciola gigantica: Giant leaf-like fluke with cephalic cone, branched caeca, and branched testes.

text: Identify the station and the arrowed structure:
options: Echinococcus granulosus scolex - rostellum with hooks
Taenia saginata scolex - rostellum with hooks
Taenia solium scolex - rostellum with hooks
explanation: Criteria of Identification: The gravid segment of Taenia solium contains a central longitudinal uterine stem giving off only 7 to 12 thick primary lateral branches on each side, which branch dendritically.
keyConcept: Taenia solium gravid segment: 7–12 lateral uterine branches per side (tree-like / dendritic).

text: Finding this egg in a stool sample does NOT identify the species of the infecting worm. Interpret.
options: The egg is passed unembryonated, so the hexacanth embryo cannot be examined
The striated shell is dissolved by stool preservatives before examination
Eggs of T. saginata and T. solium are morphologically identical, so the gravid segment or scolex is needed
The egg is identical to the H. nana egg, which is the commonest cause
Eggs of T. solium are passed only in patients with cysticercosis
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Ascaris lumbricoides is the largest intestinal nematode of humans (females 20–35 cm, males 15–30 cm with curved tail), pale pink/creamy white, cylindrical with pointed ends, bearing three sensory lips around the anterior mouth.
keyConcept: Ascaris lumbricoides adult: Giant creamy cylindrical roundworm with three anterior sensory lips.

text: This snail is the first intermediate host of:
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Lymnaea cailliaudi (Lymnaea natalensis) is a freshwater snail with a conical, dextral spiral shell that serves as the intermediate host of Fasciola hepatica and Fasciola gigantica in Egypt.
keyConcept: Lymnaea cailliaudi: Freshwater dextral conical snail, essential host of Fasciola.

text: A 4-year-old child has pruritus ani, insomnia and nocturnal enuresis. Which figure represents the stage recovered by perianal swab?
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Nocturnal perianal pruritus (pruritus ani), restlessness, and sleep disturbances in young children are caused by migrating female Enterobius vermicularis worms discharging eggs onto the perianal skin.
keyConcept: Pruritus ani and sleep disturbance in young children = Enterobius vermicularis (pinworm).

text: A 4-year-old child has diarrhea with pale, loose, offensive, fatty stools and no mucus or blood. Which figure represents the stage found in a fresh diarrheic stool?
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Pale, frothy, greasy, malodorous diarrhea floating in water (steatorrhea) accompanied by abdominal distension and flatulence is the hallmark of Giardia lamblia duodenitis / malabsorption.
keyConcept: Pale greasy floating diarrhea (steatorrhea) + flatulence = Giardia lamblia trophozoites.

text: All of the following eggs are passed immature EXCEPT:
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Enterobius vermicularis eggs are fully embryonated (mature) when deposited, whereas Ascaris, Trichuris, and Fasciola eggs are passed unembryonated (immature).
keyConcept: Enterobius eggs are passed fully mature; Ascaris, Trichuris, and Fasciola eggs are immature.

text: Structure 2 in this segment is the:
explanation: Criteria of Identification: The lateral fields of Fasciola are densely packed with highly branched, granular vitelline follicles extending from the ventral sucker to the posterior tip of the fluke.
keyConcept: Lateral fields of Fasciola are occupied by extensive branched follicular vitelline glands.

text: Finding this egg in a single stool sample does not always mean active infection. Interpret.
options: The egg is a degenerated form that has lost its operculum
The egg is shed only in the acute (invasive) stage of the disease
The egg may pass transiently after eating infected raw liver , so stool is re-examined after a liver-free diet
The egg is shed only in bile, so duodenal aspirate is needed
The egg is identical to the Heterophyes egg, so serology is required
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Finding Fasciola eggs in a single stool sample does not necessarily prove active hepatic infection; it may represent spurious (false) infection following the ingestion of cooked or raw infected sheep or cattle liver containing unabsorbed passing eggs. Re-examination after a 3-day liver-free diet confirms true infection.
keyConcept: Spurious Fasciola infection: Liver ingestion causes false-positive stool eggs; repeat after 3-day liver-free diet.

text: The arrowed structure in this larva is the:
explanation: Criteria of Identification: The rhabditiform larva of nematodes features a characteristic muscular rhabditiform esophagus consisting of an anterior cylindrical corpus, a constricted isthmus, and a swollen posterior bulb.
keyConcept: Rhabditiform larva possesses a muscular esophagus with a posterior spherical bulb.

text: Identify the specimen and the feature indicated by the lower arrow:
options: Strongyloides stercoralis female - tapering posterior end
Trichocephalus trichiurus female - blunt posterior end
explanation: Criteria of Identification: The male hookworm is recognized by its broad, fan-like copulatory bursa supported by rays, contrasting with the simple tapering pointed tail of female worms.
keyConcept: Male hookworm tail features a specialized expanded copulatory bursa.

text: In this cyst aspirate, the arrowed structures are the hooks of:
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Microscopic examination of clear hydatid fluid reveals 'hydatid sand', comprising thousands of free and brood-capsule-derived invaginated protoscolices, each bearing 4 suckers and a crown of chitinous hooklets.
keyConcept: Hydatid sand consists of invaginated protoscolices and detached hooklets from Echinococcus.

text: A child presents with appendicitis. Which figure represents the diagnostic stage?
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Cross-section of vermiform appendix revealing cross-sections of Enterobius vermicularis worms with pointed lateral cuticular crests inside the appendiceal lumen.
keyConcept: Enterobius vermicularis in appendiceal cross-section showing characteristic lateral cuticular crests.

text: Identify the station and the arrowed structure:
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Immature and mature cysts of Entamoeba histolytica frequently contain cylindrical, rod-like chromatoid bodies with characteristically blunt, rounded, cigar-shaped ends (condensed RNA/ribosomes).
keyConcept: Entamoeba histolytica chromatoid bodies have blunt, rounded, cigar-shaped ends.

text: Identify the egg and the source of infection:
options: Heterophyes heterophyes egg - raw or undercooked fish
Fasciola egg - raw or undercooked fish
Heterophyes heterophyes egg - aquatic plants such as watercress
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Heterophyes heterophyes eggs are small (28–30 × 15–17 µm), operculated, yellowish-brown with a light bulb appearance. Human infection results from consuming raw, insufficiently salted, or undercooked brackish-water fish (e.g., Fesikh, mullet, tilapia) containing encysted metacercariae.
keyConcept: Heterophyes heterophyes: Ingestion of raw/pickled brackish fish (Fesikh) containing metacercariae.

text: This parasite can be transmitted to humans by autoinfection. Yes or No? Justify.
options: No - this parasite infects only by larval skin penetration
Yes - the egg is infective on passage and is carried from the anus to the mouth
No - the egg can only infect after passing through Cyclops
Yes - the egg hatches in the small intestine and the larva migrates through the lungs again
No - the egg is passed with a one-cell ovum and needs about 2-3 weeks in soil to become embryonated
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Strongyloides stercoralis undergoes internal autoinfection: non-infective rhabditiform larvae in the intestinal lumen can molt into infective filariform larvae before excretion. These filariform larvae immediately penetrate the perianal skin or colonic mucosa, entering the circulation to perpetuate infection for decades.
keyConcept: Strongyloides stercoralis causes internal autoinfection when rhabditiform larvae molt into filariform larvae in the gut.

text: The stage found inside this egg is:
explanation: Criteria of Identification: The egg of Enterobius vermicularis contains a fully developed, coiled, tadpole-like vermiform larva when shed onto perianal skin.
keyConcept: Enterobius vermicularis egg contains a fully formed mature larva.

text: Structure 2 in this egg is the:
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Structure 2 represents the thick, irregular, tuberculated mamillated albuminous coat secreted by the uterine wall, which stains golden-brown from fecal bile pigments.
keyConcept: Ascaris outer shell: Coarse, uneven, bile-stained mamillated albuminous coat.

text: Layer 1 in this section is the:
explanation: Criteria of Identification: The wall of a hydatid cyst comprises an outer host-derived fibrous capsule (pericyst), a middle thick, milky-white, acellular laminated cuticular layer (ectocyst), and an inner thin, nucleated cellular germinal layer (endocyst) that buds off brood capsules.
keyConcept: Hydatid cyst wall: Outer acellular laminated layer and inner nucleated germinal layer.

text: The stage found inside this egg is:
explanation: Criteria of Identification: The fertilized Ascaris egg contains an unsegmented spherical one-cell ovum surrounded by a clear perivitelline space at each pole.
keyConcept: Fertilized Ascaris egg contains an unsegmented one-cell zygote.

text: This worm came out through the nose of a child after general anesthesia. Which figure represents the stage found on his stool examination?
explanation: Criteria of Identification: In high fevers, anesthesia, or anthelmintic irritation, adult Ascaris lumbricoides worms exhibit wandering erratic behavior, migrating retrograde into the stomach, esophagus, and emerging through the mouth or nose, or obstructing the bile duct.
keyConcept: Erratic Ascaris lumbricoides migration causes adult worms to emerge through the mouth or nostrils.

text: Identify the station. Why can man harbor this stage?
options: Cysticercus cellulosae - man can act as an intermediate host
Cysticercus cellulosae - man is infected only by eating undercooked pork
Cysticercus bovis - reverse peristalsis brings gravid segments to the stomach
Hydatid cyst - man swallows eggs from dog feces
Cysticercus bovis - man is the normal intermediate host
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Cysticercus cellulosae is the larval stage of Taenia solium. Humans act as accidental intermediate hosts when they ingest T. solium eggs (via contaminated food/water or autoinfection). Oncospheres hatch in the intestine and encyst in the brain (neurocysticercosis), subcutaneous tissues, and eye.
keyConcept: Humans develop cysticercosis by acting as intermediate hosts harboring Cysticercus cellulosae.

text: Identify the station:
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Scolex of Taenia saginata: Quadrate shape, 4 cup-like muscular suckers, lacks rostellum and hooks (unarmed).
keyConcept: Taenia saginata scolex: 4 muscular suckers, unarmed (no rostellum, no hooklets).

text: Identify the station and the arrowed part:
explanation: Criteria of Identification: The adult Echinococcus granulosus is minute (3–6 mm long) and consists of a pyriform scolex with 4 suckers and a rostellum of hooks, followed by only 3 proglottids: one immature, one mature, and one large gravid segment.
keyConcept: Echinococcus granulosus adult is 3–6 mm long with only 3 segments (immature, mature, gravid).

text: This parasitic stage is the pathogenic stage of:
explanation: Criteria of Identification: The hydatid cyst (larval stage) is the pathogenic stage responsible for human cystic echinococcosis, forming space-occupying lesions in the liver (70%) and lungs (20%).
keyConcept: Hydatid cyst is the pathogenic stage causing human echinococcosis.

text: This parasitic stage represents the infective stage of a case of:
explanation: Criteria of Identification: The thick-walled spherical oocyst (4–5 µm) containing 4 naked sporozoites is the infective stage of Cryptosporidium parvum, excreted in feces and resistant to chlorine.
keyConcept: Cryptosporidium infective stage: Thick-walled sporulated oocyst containing 4 sporozoites.

text: The stage found inside this egg is:
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Hookworm (Ancylostoma / Necator) eggs are passed in feces at the 4 to 8 cell segmented stage (morula), surrounded by a thin, smooth, colorless shell with a wide clear space.
keyConcept: Hookworm egg is passed at the 4–8 cell segmented morula stage with a wide clear space.

text: Which feature distinguishes this fluke from Fasciola spp.?
options: Separate sexes with a gynecophoric canal
Branched intestinal caeca with a cephalic cone
Simple, unbranched intestinal caeca and no cephalic cone
A genital sucker beside the ventral sucker
A ventral sucker displaced to one side
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Unlike hermaphroditic trematodes like Fasciola (which have flattened leaf-like bodies containing both male and female organs), Schistosomes are unique flukes with separate sexes (dioecious), where the cylindrical female resides within the male's gynecophoric canal.
keyConcept: Schistosomes are dioecious (separate sexes) with male gynecophoric canal; Fasciola is hermaphroditic.

text: Autoinfection is a means of transmission of this parasite. Yes or No? Justify.
options: No - infection occurs only by skin penetration by filariform larvae
Yes - the egg hatches in the colon and the larvae re-invade the mucosa
No - man is only an accidental host of this worm
No - the egg is passed with an unsegmented ovum and must embryonate in soil before it becomes infective
Yes - the mucoid plugs dissolve on the perianal skin and release infective larvae
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Hymenolepis nana eggs can hatch inside the intestinal lumen without reaching the outside world; oncospheres penetrate the intestinal villi to form cysticercoids that return to the lumen as adult worms.
keyConcept: Hymenolepis nana autoinfection: Eggs hatch in lumen, oncospheres develop in mucosal villi.

text: The stage found inside this egg is:
options: Immature ovum surrounded by yolk cells
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Fasciola eggs are passed unembryonated, containing an unsegmented ovum surrounded by numerous yellowish-brown vitelline/yolk cells, with an indistinct opercular cap at one pole.
keyConcept: Fasciola egg contains an unsegmented ovum surrounded by granular yolk cells with an operculum.

text: The stage found inside this egg is:
explanation: Criteria of Identification: A spherical oncosphere with 6 embryonic hooklets (hexacanth embryo) enclosed in a thick, radially striated brown embryophore.
keyConcept: Taenia egg contains a hexacanth embryo with 6 hooklets inside a striated embryophore.

text: This snail is the intermediate host of:
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Biomphalaria alexandrina is a freshwater pulmonate snail with a flat, discoidal, planorbid shell that serves as the intermediate host for Schistosoma mansoni in the Nile delta and valley.
keyConcept: Biomphalaria alexandrina: Flat discoidal planorbid snail, host of Schistosoma mansoni.

text: All of the following eggs are passed mature (embryonated) EXCEPT:
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Fasciola and Ascaris eggs require external incubation in water or soil to develop, whereas Enterobius and Heterophyes eggs are passed fully mature with infective embryos.
keyConcept: Fasciola eggs are passed immature; Enterobius and Heterophyes eggs are passed mature.

text: The stage found inside this egg is:
options: Immature ovum surrounded by yolk cells
explanation: Criteria of Identification: When excreted in feces, the mature Schistosoma mansoni egg contains a fully developed, active, ciliated miracidium equipped with cephalic glands and flame cells, ready to hatch upon contact with fresh water.
keyConcept: Mature Schistosoma mansoni egg contains a fully formed, ciliated miracidium.

text: The stage found inside this egg is:
options: Immature ovum surrounded by yolk cells
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Ancylostoma and Necator eggs in fresh feces contain an unhatched segmented ovum consisting of 4 to 8 dark blastomeres (morula stage).
keyConcept: Fresh hookworm egg contains a segmented morula of 4–8 blastomeres.

text: Which of these stages can cause internal autoinfection, so that the whole life cycle is completed inside one human host?
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Hymenolepis nana and Strongyloides stercoralis are the two classic parasites capable of true internal autoinfection within the human alimentary canal.
keyConcept: Hymenolepis nana and Strongyloides stercoralis undergo internal autoinfection in the intestine.

text: A patient has pallor, puffy eyes and swollen feet. Which figure represents the stage that can be detected in his stool?
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Severe chronic Ancylostoma duodenale infection leads to severe iron deficiency anemia (pallor, fatigue) and protein-losing enteropathy (hypoalbuminemia causing dependent pedal edema and periorbital puffiness).
keyConcept: Hookworm disease causes severe microcytic anemia, hypoalbuminemia, and periorbital/pedal edema.

text: Identify the station and the type of anemia this parasite causes:
options: Anterior end of Strongyloides female - microcytic hypochromic anemia
Anterior end of Enterobius - normocytic normochromic anemia
Hookworm buccal capsule - microcytic hypochromic anemia
Hookworm buccal capsule - macrocytic megaloblastic anemia
Hookworm copulatory bursa - microcytic hypochromic anemia
explanation: Criteria of Identification: The anterior end of Ancylostoma duodenale features a bent dorsal hook-like neck and a chitinous buccal capsule with 2 pairs of curved teeth that lacerate mucosal vessels, producing severe microcytic hypochromic iron-deficiency anemia.
keyConcept: Ancylostoma duodenale: Ventral teeth in buccal capsule cause severe microcytic hypochromic anemia.

text: Autoinfection is a means of transmission of this parasite. Yes or No? Justify.
options: No - the egg must embryonate in soil for weeks
Yes - the egg is infective when passed and can hatch in the intestine, where the oncosphere develops into a cysticercoid in the villi
Yes - rhabditiform larvae become filariform larvae in the intestine
Yes - the egg needs about 6 hours on the perianal skin before it becomes infective
No - an insect intermediate host is always needed
explanation: Criteria of Identification: H. nana eggs can hatch in the small bowel; released hexacanth larvae penetrate intestinal villi, transform into cysticercoids, and emerge into the lumen to attach as mature adults.
keyConcept: Hymenolepis nana: Direct autoinfection via cysticercoid development in intestinal villi.

text: The stage found inside this egg is:
options: Immature ovum surrounded by yolk cells
explanation: Criteria of Identification: The viable Schistosoma mansoni egg contains a ciliated miracidium with prominent apical papilla and primitive gut.
keyConcept: Schistosoma mansoni egg contains an active ciliated miracidium.

text: The snail that harbors the larval stages of this parasite is:
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Lymnaea cailliaudi harbors the sporocyst, rediae, and cercarial stages of Fasciola flukes in Egypt.
keyConcept: Lymnaea cailliaudi supports sporocyst, rediae, and cercarial development of Fasciola.

text: Fatal hyperinfection with this parasite can occur in patients on corticosteroids. Interpret.
options: Eggs hatch in the stomach and release thousands of larvae
Larvae encyst in muscles and are released by steroids
Rhabditiform larvae turn into filariform larvae inside the gut and re-invade (autoinfection), so the worm load rises sharply when immunity falls
Adult worms multiply asexually in the liver
Steroids stimulate the female to lay unembryonated eggs
explanation: Criteria of Identification: In immunocompromised patients or those receiving systemic corticosteroids, Strongyloides internal autoinfection accelerates uncontrollably into 'hyperinfection syndrome' and disseminated strongyloidiasis: millions of filariform larvae penetrate the bowel wall and invade the lungs, liver, and brain, carrying enteric Gram-negative bacteria that cause fatal sepsis and meningitis.
keyConcept: Strongyloides hyperinfection: Steroid therapy triggers massive larval dissemination and fatal sepsis.

text: Identify the egg and its arrowed content:
explanation: Criteria of Identification: A decorticated fertilized Ascaris egg lacks the rough brown mamillated albuminous coat (lost during passage or preparation), revealing a smooth, thick, transparent shell enclosing a single unsegmented ovum with crescentic spaces at both poles.
keyConcept: Decorticated Ascaris egg: Smooth colorless shell enclosing a single unsegmented ovum.
